rationale: bugs_open/153: the build/deploy contract's second half is unperformable. The makefile states (makefile:106-108) that push-*/deploy-* are git-blind by design and that 'Provenance is got right HERE, at build time, and verified against the running pod (never git, never the tag).' The first half is honoured — ref_build git-archives a committed ref so no WIP can enter an image. The second half cannot be done at all, because nothing in the image or the binary says what commit built it: measured on the live v1.0.1279 chassis pods today (2026-08-10), 'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -cE "v1\.0\.1[0-9]{3}"' returns 0 and a 40-hex sha grep returns 0; grep -c ldflags across build/docker/backend/*.dockerfile and the makefile returns 0. So bumping IMAGE_TAG and running push+deploy WITHOUT build produces a retag of the previous binary and nothing in the system can detect it — verify-agent-images (makefile:2108) compares the tag across four places and prints all-green on exactly this defect, because every one of them genuinely does say the new tag. In place of provenance the fleet hand-picks a marker string per fix and greps it in the pod. That practice is itself defective: 153's CONTRIBUTION section records three false readings in one day across two sessions, from markers that were a Go comment, prose from a workstream README, and a deleted string that survived as a PREFIX of its replacement. This change stamps the full commit sha that ref_build ALREADY COMPUTES (makefile:119, currently computed only to echo it and then discarded) into every backend binary via -ldflags into a new pkg/buildinfo, and onto every image via the OCI org.opencontainers.image.revision label, then teaches verify-agent-images to print both. 'What is running?' becomes one exact grep for a known sha, with a real negative control, instead of a hand-chosen marker hunt. The change is additive and inert until read — it adds a new mechanism rather than altering what any existing shared mechanism guarantees, so per the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 it belongs at this gate rather than in an architecture RFC.

plan.summary: Backend images and binaries carry zero build provenance, so a tag bump that skips the rebuild ships a stale binary undetectably, and every 'did my fix ship?' check degrades to hand-picked marker grepping (which has produced measured false readings). This change adds pkg/buildinfo with a single GitCommit var, has the makefile's two build macros (ref_build, tree_build) pass the commit they already compute as --build-arg GIT_COMMIT plus OCI revision/created labels, has all 14 backend Dockerfiles accept that ARG and stamp it via -ldflags, has all 14 mains log it once at startup (which is also what forces the package to be linked so -X takes effect), and widens verify-agent-images to print the local image label and the pod binary's stamp. Detects and makes verifiable; deliberately does not gate — refusing a mismatched push is candidate 2/3 in the bug file and is deferred for owner sign-off because it changes the push contract fleet-wide.

edits.rationale: The stamp target. A separate tiny package rather than main.GitCommit so ONE -ldflags string is identical across all 14 Dockerfiles regardless of each service's main-package build style — two of them (git-adapter, remote-job-spawner) build a bare main.go by filename, where a main-package -X path is fragile. Purely additive and inert: nothing reads it except the startup log line.

ref_build already computes the sha at makefile:119 purely to echo it, then throws it away. Capture it once inside the existing && chain (after the ref-verify guard has already proven REF is a commit) and pass it to docker. Full 40-hex, not --short: the bug file's own positive control is 'the pod must report exactly git rev-parse HEAD of the ref built', and 40-hex is currently a measured-zero pattern in the binary so post-fix extraction is unambiguous. Labels go on the CLI, not in the Dockerfiles, so every image built through this macro gets provenance even where a Dockerfile edit was missed — including the two CronJob images that also call ref_build and are out of scope for the Dockerfile half.
edits.sketch:
@CTX=$$(mktemp -d /tmp/ref-ctx-$(1).XXXXXX) && \
trap 'rm -rf "$$CTX"' EXIT && \
GIT_COMMIT=$$(git rev-parse '$(REF)^{commit}') && \
git archive $(REF) | tar -x -C "$$CTX" && \
docker build -t $(REGISTRY)/$(1):$(IMAGE_TAG) \
	--build-arg GIT_COMMIT=$$GIT_COMMIT \
	--label org.opencontainers.image.revision=$$GIT_COMMIT \
	--label org.opencontainers.image.created=$$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
	-f "$$CTX/build/docker/backend/$(1).dockerfile" "$$CTX"

edits.rationale: The working-tree escape hatch must NOT be able to produce an image wearing a clean commit sha — that would be worse than no provenance, since it would read as committed state to every check downstream. Stamp '<shortsha>-tree' UNCONDITIONALLY, including when git status is clean: 'porcelain was empty when the build started' is a race against the other sessions sharing this tree, not a guarantee, and a suffix that structurally cannot match a [0-9a-f]{40} grep is a simpler rule than a conditional one.
edits.sketch:
GIT_COMMIT="$$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)-tree" && \
docker build -t $(REGISTRY)/$(1):$(IMAGE_TAG) \
	--build-arg GIT_COMMIT=$$GIT_COMMIT \
	--label org.opencontainers.image.revision=$$GIT_COMMIT \
	--label org.opencontainers.image.created=$$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
	-f build/docker/backend/$(1).dockerfile .

edits.rationale: Accept the ARG and stamp it. Shown here for agent-chassis (the pilot); the IDENTICAL 2-line pattern is applied to all 14 backend Dockerfiles in this change — auth-service, core-manager, agent-chassis, reasoning-agent, web-search-adapter, web-scrape-adapter, git-adapter, image-generator-adapter, thunder-adapter, analyser-adapter, browser-runner-adapter, content-creator-agent, remote-job-spawner, kafka-scheduler. Each file's EXISTING go build flags and output path are preserved exactly (they vary: -v on reasoning-agent, no -a/-installsuffix on web-scrape-adapter and the two file-builds, -o /app/... on content-creator-agent, ./cmd/scheduler on kafka-scheduler); only the ldflags clause is inserted. ARG sits after COPY . . so changing it invalidates from the build step, not from the dependency download. browser-runner-adapter's separate playwright-cli build is deliberately untouched.
edits.sketch:
COPY . .
ARG GIT_COMMIT=unknown
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -a -installsuffix cgo \
    -ldflags "-X github.com/gqls/agentchassis/pkg/buildinfo.GitCommit=${GIT_COMMIT}" \
    -o agent-chassis ./cmd/agent-chassis

edits.rationale: LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic: -X against a package that is not linked into the binary is SILENTLY IGNORED, so without an actual import the stamp would never appear and the whole change would be inert while looking complete. One import plus one log line immediately after the existing 'defer appLogger.Sync()'. Shown for agent-chassis; the same line is applied to all 14 mains with the same message string and field key so one fleet-wide log query finds every service. Twelve use platform/logger's appLogger; remote-job-spawner uses zap.NewProduction directly and cmd/scheduler uses its own buildLogger() — those two get the identical line against their own logger variable. Note cmd/git-adapter/main.go has a second, dead mainSimple() with an identical 'defer appLogger.Sync()'; only the real main() is edited.
edits.sketch:
"github.com/gqls/agentchassis/pkg/buildinfo"
...
	defer appLogger.Sync()
	appLogger.Info("build provenance", zap.String("git_commit", buildinfo.GitCommit))

edits.rationale: The target that is structurally blind to this defect today — it compares the tag across four places and prints all-green precisely when a retag has happened. Add three read-only, fail-soft stanzas so it also shows the local image's revision label, the sha actually baked into the running pod's binary, and each pod's imageID+startTime. Every stanza is '|| echo'-guarded so the target still cannot fail; the pre-fix message names the bug so an unstamped image reads as a known state rather than a broken check. This DETECTS; it deliberately does not gate.

grounded_in: makefile:106-108 — 'push-*/deploy-* are git-blind — they ship whatever is tagged $(IMAGE_TAG). Provenance is got right HERE, at build time, and verified against the running pod (never git, never the tag).'

makefile:119 — '@echo "$(GREEN)Building $(1) from committed ref $(REF) = $$(git rev-parse --short $(REF)) — working tree NOT included.$(NC)"' — the commit is already in hand at build time and is discarded after the echo.

bugs_open/153 §Root cause — 'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -cE "v1\.0\.1[0-9]{3}" -> 0' and 'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -cE "\b[0-9a-f]{40}\b" -> 0'; 'build/docker/backend/agent-chassis.dockerfile has no ldflags, no ARG, no LABEL. The binary cannot say what it was built from, and neither can the image.'

bugs_open/153 §Why the machinery we already own does not catch this — 'On this exact defect it prints all-green, because every one of those places genuinely does say v1.0.1202. That is worth stating plainly: the one verification target we have is structurally blind to this failure, so "we checked" has been true and useless simultaneously.'

bugs_open/153 §CONTRIBUTION 4 — 'Fix candidate 1 gets stronger, not weaker. Every failure above is a per-fix marker being hand-chosen wrongly, three times, by two sessions, in one day. Stamping the commit sha into the binary retires the entire practice.'

Re-measured by this lane on 2026-08-10 against live pods agent-chassis-8496665bb8-f6svp/-sskxd on v1.0.1279: version-string grep 0, 40-hex sha grep 0, and grep -c ldflags on the chassis dockerfile and makefile both 0 — the defect is unchanged 12 days after filing and 77 tag versions on.

Mechanism proven before submission, with a negative control, against a clean git-archive of HEAD plus these edits: building cmd/agent-chassis WITH the ldflags clause yields 3 occurrences of the injected sha in the binary; building the SAME source WITHOUT it yields 0 for that sha and 1 for the literal 'unknown'. Repeated on the two bare-main.go file-builds (git-adapter, remote-job-spawner) and cmd/scheduler: 3 occurrences each.
plan.risks: 1) The two CronJob images (component-render-check, shared-output-fields-check) also call ref_build but get no Dockerfile edit this round, so docker will warn that GIT_COMMIT was not consumed — cosmetic, and they still gain the image labels; widening to them is deliberately out of scope. 2) -X is silently ignored if pkg/buildinfo is not linked in, so a service whose main.go edit was missed would build green and stamp nothing; mitigated by the pilot's pod-level positive+negative control and by all 14 mains being edited in the same change. 3) Only agent-chassis is rebuilt and rolled by this lane; the other 13 carry the edits inertly until their next normal roll, so a reviewer should expect the fleet to be mixed for a while and should NOT read an unstamped adapter as a failed fix. 4) tree_build's unconditional '-tree' suffix means a working-tree build of a clean tree is also marked -tree; that is intended (a clean-at-start check is a race on this shared tree), but it does mean the marker says 'how it was built', not 'whether the tree was dirty'. 5) verify-agent-images' new pod stanza hardcodes /app/agent-chassis and the agent-chassis deployment — correct for that service, not a general-purpose fleet check; the binary path genuinely varies across services (/root/git-adapter, /remote-job-spawner). 6) No behaviour change to any running service beyond one extra INFO log line at startup; no config, schema, or data is touched. 7) Deliberately NOT taken and named as deferred: candidate 2 (make the tag imply the build) and candidate 3 (gate push on a build stamp) — both change the push/deploy contract fleet-wide and want explicit owner sign-off; this change is their prerequisite, since the label a refusal would compare against does not exist until now.
